title: A mysterious object fell from the sky onto a Minnesota farm, and its origins remain unclear

content:
CLINTON, ILLINOIS - JULY 24: An aerial view shows corn growing in a farm field on July 24, 2025 near Clinton, Illinois. As temperatures in the Midwest climb into the mid to high 90s this week, a phenomenon called “corn sweat” in farm country helps drive up humidity, pushing dew points into the mid to high 70s. (Photo by Scott Olson/Getty Images)

A farmer in Minnesota made a strange discovery in a cornfield on October 14. The object was about 11 feet wide, made of metal and appeared burnt. It did not look like any farm equipment, so the farmer contacted the authorities.

According to the Stevens County Minnesota Sheriff's Office, state and federal agencies are investigating the object to find out where it came from, who owns it and how it can be removed safely.

How was the object found on the Minnesota farm?

On the 14th of October, the Stevens County Sheriff's Office located in western Minnesota was alerted by a farmer who had discovered the thing in his cornfields. This particular locality is approximately 240 km northwest of Minneapolis.

The deputies who went to the scene stated that this object appeared to be “a large metallic object”. They also referred to it as “a presumed object from space” which had entered the planet's atmosphere.

Local and federal authorities have been invited to investigate the object and remove it from the private property.

The sheriff's office also said there was no danger to people living nearby.

"Agency officials have determined that there is no danger to the public due to this incident," the sheriff's office said.

Could the object be part of a Chinese rocket?

No one has pinpointed the precise origin of the debris. Nevertheless, some scientists think it may belong to the upper stage of the Zhuque-2E rocket, according to a space industry magazine.

The rocket launched in September with the aim of putting satellites into orbit. Its upper stage has a diameter similar to that of the piece found in Minnesota. The upper stage is a rocket component that continues its journey after the first stages disengage.

Information provided by the media indicates that the upper stage of the rocket re-entered the atmosphere above the Midwest region. The locals reported that the object had a unique serial number and had been lying in the farmer's field for six weeks.

Nonetheless, any information that the object belonged to the rocket is still unverified.

Why is falling space debris a concern?

Falling pieces of space equipment will happen more and more as the number of satellite launches increases. Most of them get burnt in the atmosphere, while the rest land on remote places. While uncontrolled landings are rare and rarely injure anyone, that does not stop debris from falling.

A case from July 2026 can serve as an example: some metal spheres located on the Australian coast were said to be linked to the rocket. As for the Minnesota object, it is still being investigated, and it is still unknown where it comes from.
